# Wisdom of Solomon Chapter 4 — Disagreement Log

**Date:** 2026-03-17
**Agents:** EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA
**Total Disagreements:** 13

---

## Disagreement 1 — Verse 1: structure of the opening comparison

- **EMET:** "Better is childlessness with virtue, for immortality is in the memory of virtue"
- **LOGOS:** "Better is childlessness with virtue; for there is immortality in the memory of virtue"
- **PNEUMA:** "A life of virtue without children is better than a large family without virtue"
- **Resolution:** SOPHIA adopts LOGOS — the semi-colon preserves the two-clause structure; PNEUMA's expansion adds "large family" which is not in the text.

---

## Disagreement 2 — Verse 2: crown/triumph metaphor

- **EMET:** "it marches crowned in triumph, victorious in the contest for prizes that are undefiled"
- **LOGOS:** "crowned in triumph throughout all ages, it wins the prize in the contest for what is undefiled"
- **PNEUMA:** "virtue moves crowned and victorious — winning in every undefiled contest"
- **Resolution:** SOPHIA adopts LOGOS — "wins the prize" (athlophoros) is precise; EMET's "marches" adds a military image not present; PNEUMA's "every undefiled contest" is paraphrastic.

---

## Disagreement 3 — Verse 3: "prolific brood" vs. "prolific offspring"

- **EMET:** "the prolific brood of the ungodly"
- **LOGOS:** "the prolific offspring of the ungodly"
- **PNEUMA:** "the ungodly may produce many children"
- **Resolution:** SOPHIA adopts "prolific offspring" — "brood" (EMET) has negative connotations in English that go beyond the Greek polugonos; "offspring" is neutral and precise.

---

## Disagreement 4 — Verse 4: "put out branches in season" vs. "flourish for a time"

- **EMET:** "even if they put out branches in season"
- **LOGOS:** "even if they flourish for a time"
- **PNEUMA:** "let them put out growth for a season"
- **Resolution:** SOPHIA adopts "flourish for a time" (LOGOS) — thallontōn means "sprouting/flourishing"; "put out branches" is overly literal and dendrological; PNEUMA's "growth" is acceptable but vague.

---

## Disagreement 5 — Verse 6: "examined" vs. "called to account"

- **EMET:** "when they are examined" (exetazomenōn)
- **LOGOS:** "when they are called to account"
- **PNEUMA:** "when the time of accounting arrives"
- **Resolution:** SOPHIA adopts "called to account" — exetazō means to examine/investigate closely; "called to account" conveys the juridical connotation; PNEUMA slightly depersonalizes.

---

## Disagreement 6 — Verse 8: formulation of the "old age" principle

- **EMET:** "old age is not honored for length of time"
- **LOGOS:** "honorable old age is not a matter of length of time"
- **PNEUMA:** "Old age is not something earned by accumulating years"
- **Resolution:** SOPHIA adopts LOGOS — "honorable old age" as subject makes the argument clearest; PNEUMA's "earned by accumulating" is a strong paraphrase.

---

## Disagreement 7 — Verse 10: "taken up" vs. "translated" vs. "taken away"

- **EMET:** "he was taken up"
- **LOGOS:** "he was translated"
- **PNEUMA:** "he was taken away"
- **Resolution:** SOPHIA adopts "taken up" — the Enoch allusion (metetethe, LXX Gen 5:24) is most recognizable through "taken up" in English theological tradition; "translated" is archaic; "taken away" lacks the theological precision.

---

## Disagreement 8 — Verse 11: "alter his understanding" vs. "pervert his understanding"

- **EMET:** "lest wickedness alter his understanding"
- **LOGOS:** "lest wickedness pervert his understanding"
- **PNEUMA:** "before wickedness could warp his judgment"
- **Resolution:** SOPHIA adopts "pervert his understanding" — alloiōsē means to alter/change; but in moral context the change is degradation/perversion; PNEUMA's "warp" is vivid but colloquial.

---

## Disagreement 9 — Verse 12: goēteia rendering

- **EMET:** "the fascination of wickedness" (general)
- **LOGOS:** "the bewitchment of trivial things" (phaulos = trivial/worthless)
- **PNEUMA:** "the spell that trivial things cast over us"
- **Resolution:** SOPHIA adopts "the bewitchment of trivial things" (LOGOS) — goēteia is specifically enchantment/sorcery; "fascination" (EMET) is too weak; PNEUMA's circumlocution loses the noun's force.

---

## Disagreement 10 — Verse 14: divine motivation for the taking

- **EMET:** "therefore he took him quickly from the midst of wickedness"
- **LOGOS:** "therefore the Lord took him quickly out from the midst of wickedness"
- **PNEUMA:** "the Lord, out of love, quickly removed him from the midst of wickedness"
- **Resolution:** SOPHIA adopts LOGOS — the subject "the Lord" needs to be explicit; PNEUMA adds "out of love" which is interpretive and not in the Greek text.

---

## Disagreement 11 — Verse 18: "hold him in contempt" vs. "despise" vs. "sneer"

- **EMET:** "they will hold him in contempt"
- **LOGOS:** "they will despise him"
- **PNEUMA:** "they will sneer at him — and God will sneer back"
- **Resolution:** SOPHIA adopts "despise" (LOGOS) — kataphronēsousin is the standard term; PNEUMA's double "sneer" is rhetorically effective but too colloquial; EMET's "hold in contempt" is fine but slightly cumbersome.

---

## Disagreement 12 — Verse 19: "shatter them speechless" vs. "dash them down speechless"

- **EMET:** "he will shatter them speechless and headlong"
- **LOGOS:** "the Lord will dash them down speechless and shattered"
- **PNEUMA:** "God will shatter them into silence"
- **Resolution:** SOPHIA adopts LOGOS — "dash down" captures the rhipsē (hurling down) motion; "shattered" is then the result; EMET's "headlong" adds a posture not in the Greek; PNEUMA loses the physical violence.

---

## Disagreement 13 — Verse 20: "confront them to their face" vs. "convict them to their face"

- **EMET:** "their lawless deeds will convict them to their face"
- **LOGOS:** "their lawless deeds will confront them to their face"
- **PNEUMA:** "brought before them, right to their face"
- **Resolution:** SOPHIA adopts "confront them to their face" — antikatastēsontai means to stand over against/confront; the confrontation image is clear; EMET's "convict" moves toward a judicial verdict not quite in the verb.
